summary: I wrote a new simulator that does not use the original correlator code (`repl_lib.py`). It has two engines: a dense one built from 4x4 expm pair unitaries embedded by bit manipulation, and a Pauli-transfer-matrix engine storing all 4^N coefficients. Its results match the stored file 1UBQ_p19_N10_o0_g0.json to machine precision [MEASURED]: S_exact within 8e-15, F_exact within 4e-14, and FI_t and FI_otoc_t within 1.6e-11 of their peak. Its eps=1e-4 sparse-Pauli run gives the same string count at all 17 records, the same bias to 9e-14, and the same failure times (transfer 17, echo 4) [MEASURED]. The stored numbers are therefore correct. Halving the finite-difference step changes FI by at most 2%, and switching to continuous-time dynamics changes FI by at most 4% with the late-window echo fraction unchanged (0.919 vs 0.922) [MEASURED]. The stored rigid parameter rigid_res16 duplicates radial_HA/GLU16, because the file was produced by nmr_gate.py at git 92bb4eb. analyze_nmr2.py removes the duplicate, but the fix is missing from the deviation log, and the current rigid_res2 parameter moves the probe's nearest proton, so it is not a long-range parameter [MEASURED]. The decisive finding is that the next rung of the eps ladder, eps=3e-5, reproduces the echo within sigma over the whole 320 µs window for this job (max bias 0.0075, at most 256,425 strings, matching the stored C2 run exactly), giving f_hard=0 and gain=1 [MEASURED]. The same happens for 1UBQ p245 (in the repo's own C2 data), 1PGA p390 and 1PGAHN p260 [MEASURED]. Two jobs keep part of their window at eps=3e-5: 1PGA p325 (f_hard 0.38-0.67) and 1UBQHN p548 (0.81-0.98) [MEASURED]. Across the 17 unique parameters tested, the median echo f_hard falls from 0.95 to 0.00, which is below the C3 kill threshold of 0.3. The subset is not representative and 15 parameters are untested, so C3-kill-1 is indicated, not established [DERIVED]. The C2 string metric is saturated: M*(eps=3e-5) is 0.46-0.50 of the 4^N/2 parity-allowed Pauli strings at both N=8 and N=10, so the growth from 16k to 257k strings is just the growth of the operator space [DERIVED]. It therefore cannot measure classical hardness against exact methods, and exact dense N=10 takes 12.5 CPU-s per geometry [MEASURED; the interpretation is INFERENCE]. The claim wording in D4, T6 and CURRENT_STATE ('every classical adversary/approximation tested fails') is contradicted by the repo's own eps=3e-5 data. The ranges quoted there are also slightly off: the echo/transfer FI ratio spans 3.2-183x, and f_hard^OTOC spans 0.49-1.0 [MEASURED]. The failure time also depends on implementation: truncating per Trotter step instead of per pair moves the echo failure from index 4 to 5 and f_hard from 0.92 to 0.75 for one parameter [MEASURED]. Verdict: the numbers are right, but the N=10 echo window is an artefact of where the adversary panel stopped (eps >= 1e-4). It shows that sparse Pauli dynamics cannot compress the echo, not that classical computation fails. The question at N >= 12 remains open.

lens: fi_method: attack on the Fisher-information methodology (noise model, FD step, time grid, hard-window partition, gain definition, experimental cost of time reversal, whether the parameters are meaningful)
summary:
(1) Replication is exact. fi_common.setup reproduces the gate's cluster, parameters, S, F and dF for 1UBQ_p19_N10_o0_g0 to 0.0 [MEASURED].
(2) The gate's C1 adversary panel stops at eps=1e-4. The existing C2 eps=3e-5 run reproduces the echo within sigma over the full 0-320 us window at N=10: max bias 0.0075 (p19) and 0.0068 (p245). By the gate's own criterion, f_hard^F=0 at N=10 on both dense probes [MEASURED, from RAW/nmr_sparse].
(3) The requested improved statistic works against the gate's gain. The gate's gain FI_tot/FI_easy assumes the classical analyst discards every point after t_c. An actual nonlinear least-squares fit of the truncated classical model to all exact data at N=8 gives much smaller deficits. For eps=3e-4 the fitted phi bias is -0.100/-0.003/-0.081/-0.006 A (6.0/0.6/3.9/1.3 sd), and the calibrated-RMSE gain is 36.9/1.46/16.9/2.84 against gate gains of 162/119/368/6.3. For eps=1e-3 the gain is 71/46/5.9/1.2 against 44908/491/8248/37. So the gate overstates the classical deficit by 3-5000x [MEASURED].
(4) The correct estimator-level statistic does NOT erase the window at sigma=0.01, because the echo is extremely sensitive (single-parameter CRB sd 0.004-0.04 A). Sub-sigma biases still move phi by more than 1 sd: at N=10 eps=3e-5 the Mahalanobis bias is D=1.41 (p19) and 1.17 (p245). Under D<=0.5 the C2 echo cost M*_F(N=10) is censored at >2.57e5 strings for p19. So the scaling side of the lead is not weakened by the choice of statistic [MEASURED; linearised with J_exact, which N=8 fits show overstates the bias by up to ~2x].
(5) The noise model is the decisive flaw. It uses constant sigma with perfect time reversal, but a real echo needs reversal. The NMR Loschmidt echo decays within T3 ~ T2/0.15, independently of the perturbation [LITERATURE-SUPPORTED: arXiv:2112.00607, PRA 105, 052232; abstract checked; sample and T2 convention not verified]. T2 from the Van Vleck M2 is 12-18 us dense and 28-69 us for the amide-only network [MEASURED]. With the per-job anchor T3=T2/0.15, the median joint gain (S all + F all)/(S all + F easy) falls to 1.18-1.46 dense and 1.00-1.16 HN, and the median echo/transfer FI ratio falls from 12.5 to 0.77 (dense) and 0.39 (HN) [DERIVED from stored FI]. Transferring R=0.15 to protein local OTOCs is INFERENCE.
(6) The echo was never evaluated with dephasing. At gamma=5000 and 20000 1/s, sparse eps=1e-3 and 1e-4 respectively reproduce the dephased echo over the whole window, and echo FI < transfer FI. At gamma=1000 the eps=3e-5 run closes the window. The project's own R1-E proxy gave gamma_i ~2-14e4 1/s [MEASURED].
(7) Experiment accounting: each butterfly spin needs its own perturb-and-reverse experiment (n_b=4), while transfer reads all b at once. Per experiment, the echo/transfer FI ratio is median 3.1 (not 12.5), and the joint gain is median 3.6 even without attenuation [DERIVED].
(8) The parameters are not structurally meaningful as used. They are single-proton radial moves at 3.2-3.8 A, and the stored p19 job double-counts a pre-fix duplicate parameter (rigid_res16). With the other protons' coordinates unknown, single-proton marginal CRB is 1.2-1.5 A even with all exact echo data, against 0.01-0.04 A in the gate. The hard window adds 4 of 26 coordinate directions determined to <0.1 A (10 to 14), and only 1 of 26 under T3=85 us attenuation [MEASURED FI].
(9) FD step (h=0.02-0.1) and the coarse grid are not decisive: <1% change at N=10, and f_hard -2 to -10 points on the fine grid [MEASURED].
Net: the window survives at the theoretical level, with gain 1.2-71x instead of up to 1e4. At the practical level it is effectively erased (median joint gain ~1.0-1.5), conditional on the attenuation anchor.

lens: classical_front: strongest new classical adversaries for the echo (first-order OTOC) F_ab(t) at N=10, t in [80, 320] us
summary:
Four new estimator families were tested against a self-computed sector-exact reference on 1UBQ p19, 1UBQ p245 and 1PGA p390 (N=10, orientation 0, gamma=0, bs=[1,7,8,9]). None reaches t_c >= 160 us on all clusters at polynomial cost, and none beats the panel's 80 us at polynomial cost. The kill rule did not fire [MEASURED].

E1, the cluster-correlation expansion of the OTOC (additive and multiplicative, all orders from one table of 480 sub-cluster simulations), gives t_c = 40-60 us at orders k<=4 (sub-clusters of <=6 spins). It reaches 80-120 us only at order k=7 (9 of 10 spins, order N-3, not polynomial). At N=8, order N-3 also fails at 60-100 us [MEASURED].

E2, the operator-spreading stochastic model (incoherent Pauli-path Markov chain and its mean-field/FKPP closure), fails at 20 us with errors 0.3-0.9. Calibrating its rate and memory time on N=8 exact data of the same probe does not help [MEASURED]. The mechanism is that dropping path cross-terms turns coherent operator growth into diffusion [DERIVED].

E3, sparse Pauli propagation with unbiased stochastic reinsertion (independent replica pairs), fails at 40 us from a sign problem: errors 1e2-1e3 at 40 us for M=3e3-1e4 [MEASURED]. The uncapped variant keeps about ||O||_1/eps strings and was stopped at the 10 CPU-min limit without producing a record [MEASURED].

E4, an MPO/operator-TEBD tensor network with exact Pauli-transfer gates and SWAP routing (validated at N=6 to 5e-7), fails at 40 us for chi=16, 32 and 64. The summed discarded weight is about 1 even at chi=64 [MEASURED].

For context, the panel's sparse Pauli at eps=3e-5 (existing C2 RAW) is within 0.01 over the whole window on p19 and p245. It needs 2.4-2.6e5 strings, about 4^10/4, the full symmetry-allowed operator space, so it is exact simulation in disguise [MEASURED; interpretation INFERENCE].

A new light-cone diagnostic found that every one of the 9 non-probe spins shifts F_ab by more than 0.01 at 20-160 us (leave-one-out), so no sub-cluster decomposition can work [MEASURED]. The N=10 exact echo is also not converged in cluster size: adding the 11th and 12th nearest protons changes it by more than 0.01 from 40-120 us, and by up to 0.14 (14 sigma) inside [80, 320] us [MEASURED]. So the 80 us classical-approximation failure falls where the echo's dependency set outgrows the 10-spin cluster. The physical window signal involves at least 12 spins, and the decisive comparator for it is exact light-cone simulation, not the approximations tested here [INFERENCE].

Verdict: KILLS R1 at the practical level, conditional on one number carrying over from model solids to proteins.

1. The informative echo window sits at or after the point where physical time reversal fails. Measured in the isolated cluster's own T2 = 1/sqrt(M2), the classical-failure time is t_c* = 3.8–17 T2 and the echo-FI midpoint is t_50 = 4.8–25 T2 (median about 10) [MEASURED, scales.json]. Measured reversal horizons in dipolar solids are T3 ≈ 6.7 T2 for the best magic-echo-type Loschmidt echo (adamantane, perturbation-independent limit) and ≈ 4 T2 for a local polarization echo, the protocol a site-resolved experiment needs. Past T3 the echo decays with time constant 1.7 T2 [LIT: Sanchez, Chattah & Pastawski PRA 105, 052232 (2022), full text read; PRL 124, 030601 (2020); Zangara et al. 2016].

2. Re-weighting the RAW per-time-point echo FI by A(t)^2 [MEASURED, reversal_envelope.json]:
   - Polarization-echo envelope, most generous accounting: a median of 0.9% of the hard-window FI survives (range 5e-12 to 10%). The gain over classically usable data (transfer plus easy echo) is at most 1.32 in all 11 jobs.
   - Best-case Loschmidt-echo envelope: 2 of 11 jobs reach gain ≥ 2 with the generous cluster T2; 0 of 11 with the physical whole-network T2 (maximum 1.35).
   - Break-even needs T3/T2 ≈ 7.5 in median under generous accounting and ≈ 15 under physical accounting; 4–6.7 has been measured.
   - Mechanism [INFERENCE supported by MEASURED+LIT]: classical hardness and irreversibility both come from the same operator scrambling and are both measured in units of T2. Rescaling the couplings (dilution, deuteration, Floquet scaling) moves both windows together and cannot open a gap.

3. Independent of reversal, the forward model is wrong by more than the assumed noise σ [MEASURED in-model, N=10, exact]:
   - Methyl rotation changes the echo by 7–49 σ.
   - Realistic 1 kHz site offsets change it by 5–66 σ.
   - A backward-leg scaling mismatch of 15% (the size Sanchez 2022 measured) changes it by 23–65 σ.
   - In the amide-only network, heteronuclear local fields (15N 2.7–5.6 kHz, 14N 3.2–6.5 kHz, 2H 1.3–2.2 kHz rms) are as large as or larger than the homonuclear scale (1.7–4.2 kHz).

4. Treating offsets and the reversal mismatch as unknown nuisances leaves 21% (dense) and 2% (amide) of the hard-window structural FI with no priors, and 46% / 14% with moderate priors [MEASURED].

5. Static 1H lines are 43–47 kHz wide (dense) and 10–11 kHz (amide), so no single proton can be selected by chemical shift [MEASURED widths; INFERENCE for the shift ranges]. Site selection needs a site-specific 13C/15N label and a separately labelled sample for every (probe, butterfly) pair [LIT: the polarization-echo protocol; Zhang et al. 2510.19550].

6. At σ = 0.01 the arithmetic gives 0.23 days per time point at a per-scan single-site SNR of 1. Recovering the ideal hard-window FI for one probe takes 32–206 days (dense, best-case Loschmidt echo) or 120–1900 days (polarization echo) [MEASURED arithmetic; the SNR value is INFERENCE].

7. Several physical effects are benign [MEASURED]:
   - Static heterogeneity up to 0.2 Å keeps 80–99% of the hard-window FI.
   - A 2° mosaic spread keeps 87–99%.
   - A full powder average keeps about 56%.
   - The trouble is irreversibility and model error, not sample imperfection.

8. Weakly aligned proteins in liquid crystals cannot reach the scrambling regime (couplings too weak for the relaxation time) [INFERENCE]. Zhang et al. reach 2.5 ms forward plus 2.5 ms backward only because their molecules are finite, isolated ~10–15-spin networks [LIT]. Their protein extrapolation assumes a 1 s decoherence time, which conflicts with the T3 ≈ 30–70 µs implied here [INFERENCE].

9. Caveats:
   - T3/T2 has only been measured in adamantane, ferrocene, cymantrene and cobaltocene. No protein measurement was found [UNPROVEN transfer].
   - Dominguez et al. PRA 104, 012402 (2021) report sub-linear scaling of the decoherence rate with cluster size under weak perturbation [LIT counter-evidence, abstract level].
   - Double-quantum engineered echoes are reported to be more reversible (about 10^4 spins against 10^2 for XXZ) and remain an untested residual window (R1-DQ) [LIT+UNPROVEN].

The only anchors are worst-case: DQC1 (Knill-Laflamme 1998; DQC1-completeness of OTOCs over all eigenstates, arXiv:2411.05208, abstract-level) and universality (Cubitt-Montanaro-Piddock 2018).

summary:
I built one engine that computes many echo observables from a single simulation: exact sector/parity block diagonalisation, plus sparse Pauli propagation with a Walsh-Hadamard rebuild of the full matrix. It was validated against the C1 RAW to 1e-16 and against the stored eps=1e-4 adversary bit-for-bit (MEASURED). I tested four variants at N=10.

1. Second-order OTOC F2 = Tr[(Z_a(t) Z_b)^4]/2^N. Truncation bias is linear in the discarded norm delta for both observables: about 15-21·delta for F2 against 1.3-2.9·delta for F1 (MEASURED). So F2 fails earlier: 30-40 us vs 70-80 us at eps=1e-4 (MEASURED, 1UBQ and 1PGA).
2. The strongest pre-registered twin (eps=3e-5) reproduces S and F1 over the whole 320 us window (MEASURED by R1_replicate). F2 fails under it at 60 us (bias 2.05σ, then 3.45σ at 80 us), as the delta-law predicted before the run (MEASURED). Adding late F2 gives a quantum-only gain of only 1.65x median, 1.76x max (DERIVED).
3. That F2 window is not robust. eps=1e-5 (219k strings) reproduces F2 within 0.44σ to at least 70 us (MEASURED). F2 costs 4t of evolution against 2t for F1 (DERIVED). Per unit evolution budget, F1 gives more hard FI than F2 on 1UBQ at every budget against eps=1e-4 (MEASURED). Adding 2 environment protons moves F2 by 1.3σ/2.6σ at 80/100 us, against 0.64σ/1.0σ for F1 (MEASURED).
4. Multi-site butterflies and subset coherence-order spectra (phase-multiplexed echoes) are classically EASIER than F1: F1_multi frac_hard 0.23 vs 0.77; MQC_S never failed within 200 us and carries about 1% of F1's FI per scalar (MEASURED).
5. The pulse-engineered double-quantum Hamiltonian, which is exactly reversible by an RF phase shift (LIT-UNVERIFIED), carries 1.8-4.0x more echo FI in 0-100 us at equal pair norm, and 2.2-3.1x per measurement at matched local-T2 time (MEASURED/DERIVED). It is not harder in local-T2 units: eps=1e-4 fails at a secular-equivalent 104 us, and the faster sub-cluster failure does not replicate on 1PGA (MEASURED). It is more environment-sensitive: 2.1σ vs 0.28σ at 60 us (MEASURED).
6. Scaled flip-flop (kappa≠1) cannot be produced by global RF (DERIVED). Heteronuclear probes and multi-orientation designs offer no hardness mechanism (INFERENCE).
7. Dilution scale law: dipolar r^-3 couplings make hardness a function of R/a only (DERIVED). The classically-hard regime (>47 labelled spins) then maps onto long-range distances: 11-15 Å for amide-only, 15-18 Å for ILV methyls, about 25 Å for 1 label per 10 residues, against about 6 Å for dense 1H (DERIVED from coordinates). The cost is 7.5-90x longer coherent evolution (DERIVED). Echo reversal decays on the network's own T2 (T3~T2; LITERATURE, Sánchez et al. PRL 2020), so dilution does not widen the dimensionless reversible window (INFERENCE). Failure times collapse approximately in units of the cluster rms coupling: 1.04 dense vs 1.34 amide (MEASURED).
8. Picking time points by hard FI per quantum-µs gives 2.7x (F1) / 5.4x (F2) more FI per unit evolution; this is a cost constant only (DERIVED).

Net: no variant strengthens the window beyond the originally claimed evidence. The search shows a trade-off: every lever that raises information or approximate hardness also raises environment sensitivity or depth (MEASURED at N=10). The N=10 failure time is set by adversary strength, not by a classical wall (MEASURED).

My first mechanism hypothesis, F2 bias ∝ sqrt(delta) (the Hölder bound), was wrong. The measured bias is linear in delta with an approximately 10x larger prefactor, so F2 is a constant-factor effect for truncation adversaries (MEASURED).

Levers that increase echo information (F2, the DQ Hamiltonian) also increase sensitivity to unmodelled environment protons. The embedding misfit exceeds σ 20-40 us earlier (MEASURED). This compounds the value-lens model-bias problem.
